clue.text: Some depart for Met to see this?

indicators.note: Some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A question about why some people leave for the Metropolitan Museum: what are they going to look at?
explanation.walkthrough: The Met is New York's Metropolitan Museum of Art, so the whole clue also hints at the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Paintings and sculpture, the things a museum visitor goes to see, are each a kind of creative genre.

clue.text: CIA tipped off and RAF scrambled over the continent

indicators.note: in a down clue, over puts the first piece above the second
scrambled means the letters of RAF are mixed up, as fighter planes are scrambled
tipped off suggests the letters of CIA knocked over into a new order

explanation.surface: American intelligence warns British fighters, which take off over a continent.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tipped off' and 'scrambled' sound like spy and air-force jargon but both signal anagrams.
explanation.definitionFit: A large landmass of the world, home to Egypt and Kenya, is one continent.

clue.text: Can-can broadcast leaving one with large bill

indicators.note: broadcast says the words are spoken on air, so we go by how they are said

parts.note: the word can given twice is two cans

explanation.surface: The can-can dance being shown on television, leaving someone with a big bill.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Can-can' is the dance, but read as 'two can' it is said like the bird's name.
explanation.definitionFit: A tropical bird known for its enormous colourful beak, so a creature with a large bill.

clue.text: Consumed to excess, finished and died with 8, say?

parts.note: something finished is over

indicators.note: say asks us to go by the sound of the word

parts.note: 8 refers to the answer of 8 down, whose first word is used here

explanation.surface: Someone who ate too much, finished and died: a cautionary tale.
explanation.walkthrough: The first word of 8 down, the London Inn of Court, sounds like GRAZE.
explanation.definitionFit: Land eaten bare by too many animals has been overused, consumed beyond what it can bear.

clue.text: Part-time Dickens student?

indicators.note: Part says only a portion of the following words is used, a run of letters inside them

explanation.surface: A part-time student of Dickens's novels.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark admits that the answer is only a medical student by a stretch: the word is used for a doctor in training.
explanation.definitionFit: Informally, someone studying medicine is called this, as well as a qualified doctor.

clue.text: Giving speech terrible review?

parts.note: a score of zero, written O, is as terrible as a mark can be
a rating is a reviewer's verdict or score

explanation.surface: A critic panning a lecture: the talk got a terrible write-up.
explanation.walkthrough: Read as one phrase, an 'O rating' is a nought-out-of-ten review, which is what makes the clue's question mark fair.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone delivering a formal address or declaiming to an audience is giving a speech.

clue.text: 1Direction recorded Right Now's intro after 17 — sexy stuff

indicators.note: after says the first letter of Now comes following the previous piece
recorded says the words are heard as on a recording, going by sound

parts.note: one direction, one of the compass points, is east
17 points to 17 down, whose first word, a three-letter self-regard, appears here with its letters rearranged

indicators.note: intro picks the opening letter of Now's

explanation.surface: The boy band One Direction cut a single, Right Now, that is pure sex appeal.
explanation.walkthrough: One Direction is a boy band and Right Now one of its songs. The setter's link to 17 is loose: its first word gives OGE only when rearranged, with no word to say so.
explanation.definitionFit: A female sex hormone can loosely be called sexy stuff, the chemical behind desire.

clue.text: Essentially James Naughtie's fronting Last Word

indicators.note: essentially points to the core of James, without its first and last letters
fronting picks the first letter of Naughtie's

explanation.surface: Radio presenter James Naughtie hosting a programme called Last Word.
explanation.walkthrough: James Naughtie is a long-serving BBC radio presenter; Last Word is a BBC Radio 4 obituary programme.
explanation.definitionFit: The closing utterance of a prayer or hymn, so the last word spoken.

clue.text: Minions — a DESPICABLE ME feature

indicators.note: despicable suggests the letters are treated badly, knocked out of order

explanation.surface: The Minions are a feature of the film Despicable Me.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ME' is not the pronoun from the film title but myalgic encephalomyelitis, chronic fatigue syndrome.
explanation.definitionFit: Sleeplessness is a common symptom of chronic fatigue syndrome, so a feature of that illness.

clue.text: Not quite white lie perhaps to name lawyers' whereabouts

parts.note: a grey shade is not quite white, here in the American spelling
telling a lie is one example of a sin

explanation.surface: A white lie told to protect someone's name.
explanation.walkthrough: Gray's Inn is one of the four Inns of Court in London, the professional bodies for barristers.
explanation.definitionFit: One of London's Inns of Court is where barristers have their chambers, so a home of lawyers.

clue.text: Bat on continuously before this in US in cover?

definitions.text: Bat on continuously before this in US
definitions.meaning: the words 'Bat on' run together as one word make BATON, and placed before the answer they name Baton ..., the city in Louisiana
make-up such as blusher covers the cheeks

explanation.surface: A cricketer told to keep batting, wondering what protective cover is needed in America.
explanation.definitionFit: Red powder or cream applied to the cheeks is a cosmetic cover, a kind of make-up.

clue.text: Days struggling over drink problem

indicators.note: over is used here for one piece lying over the other on both sides, enclosing it
struggling suggests the letters of Days thrashing about into a new order

parts.note: Pepsi is a well-known fizzy drink

explanation.surface: Several days of battling a drinking problem.
explanation.walkthrough: 'over' here means wrapped around, not on top of: the reworked days enclose the drink.
explanation.definitionFit: Indigestion is a stomach complaint, so a medical problem.

clue.text: Plastic explosive planted next to Queen, perhaps?

parts.note: an explosive charge is the bomb itself
a queen is one example of a playing card

explanation.surface: A plastic explosive bomb planted beside the monarch: an assassination plot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Plastic' seems to describe the explosive, but it is the definition: plastic is slang for credit cards.
explanation.definitionFit: Plastic is everyday slang for payment cards, and this is one such card used to buy on account.

clue.text: Bemused after removing bed and finding these?

indicators.note: after removing tells us to take letters out of the word Bemused

parts.note: the letters of bed, found scattered through Bemused in the same order

explanation.surface: Someone puzzled after the bed is taken away, then finding something unexpected.
explanation.walkthrough: The B, the second E and the D of BEMUSED go, leaving the birds; 'these' points to what is found in the word.
explanation.definitionFit: The pronoun stands for the birds that are left over, large flightless Australian runners.

clue.text: Organisation of football show in US quite a bit after Dead Ringers

parts.note: the FA is the Football Association, which runs English football
CSI is an American television crime drama
miles means a great deal, as in miles better

explanation.surface: Arranging football coverage on American TV some time after the comedy show Dead Ringers.
explanation.walkthrough: Dead Ringers is a BBC impressions comedy show; read as a phrase, dead ringers are exact lookalikes.
explanation.definitionFit: Exact copies of documents are identical likenesses, as dead ringers are.

clue.text: Behind initially in Goodwood race meeting

parts.note: behind is a word for the backside, as is ass in American slang

indicators.note: initially picks the opening letters of the words in and Goodwood

parts.note: a race can mean a people or nation

explanation.surface: Someone at the back early on in a race at the Goodwood course.
explanation.walkthrough: Goodwood is an English racecourse in Sussex; 'race' looks like the horse race but means a people.
explanation.definitionFit: A secret rendezvous, especially between lovers, is a kind of meeting.

clue.text: Jammed finger in fridge perhaps

parts.note: the cake has jam in it and is a finger-like shape that may be kept chilled

explanation.surface: An injury: a finger caught in the fridge door.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Jammed finger' reads as an injury, but it describes a sponge cake rolled round jam.
explanation.definitionFit: A sponge cake spread with jam and rolled into a log is a jam-filled cylinder, a kind of finger.

clue.text: Jim's going — heading off to war because of this?

definitions.text: Jim's going — heading off to war because of this?

indicators.note: war suggests conflict and disorder, so the letters are thrown into a new arrangement
heading off says the first letter of going is removed

explanation.surface: Jim is leaving for the front, perhaps driven by patriotic fervour.
explanation.walkthrough: 'heading off' drops the G of GOING to leave OING, which is mixed with JIMS.
explanation.definitionFit: Aggressive flag-waving patriotism is just the sentiment that sends a young man marching to battle.

clue.text: They give boost, for example, to rising rents

indicators.note: in a down clue, rising means the word to is read upwards, backwards

parts.note: rents are tears or rips

explanation.surface: An example of rising rents boosting a landlord's income.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rents' looks like money paid to a landlord, but here means tears in fabric.
explanation.definitionFit: Activities done chiefly for self-gratification inflate one's sense of importance, so they boost the self.

clue.text: These needing stir?

indicators.note: These points at the letters of the words that follow, which, as the clue says, need a stir to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A cook's question about what has to be mixed.
explanation.walkthrough: The setter gives no separate anagram word: 'stir' is part of the letters and also says what to do with them, while 'These' points at the letters. The whole clue describes the answer, things a recipe has you stir.
explanation.definitionFit: The items combined in a recipe are exactly what a cook stirs together.

clue.text: Gaga's sampling from Gypsy chords

indicators.note: sampling says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Lady Gaga samples some Gypsy chords in a song.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is 'Gaga' alone: the draft's 'Gaga's' includes the 's, which stands for 'is' and links definition to wordplay. Gaga is mad, not the singer.
explanation.definitionFit: Gaga means crazy, and a psycho is informally a mad person; the setter treats the two as interchangeable.

clue.text: Creative individual's played onside

indicators.note: played suggests the letters are moved around, rearranged

explanation.surface: A creative footballer is being played onside.
explanation.walkthrough: Thomas Edison was the prolific American inventor.
explanation.definitionFit: The great American inventor is a prime example of a creative mind.

clue.text: Owner of Microsoft Windows ultimately denied access

indicators.note: denied tells us one letter is refused, taken away from the founder's name

parts.note: Bill Gates co-founded Microsoft

indicators.note: ultimately points to the last letter of Windows

explanation.surface: The Microsoft boss is locked out of his own Windows.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Windows' looks like the software, but only its final S is used.
explanation.definitionFit: A gate is an opening through which entry is gained, a means of access.

clue.text: Following agreement, Surrey's opening star half-heartedly didn't score after end of tea

indicators.note: after says the earlier pieces follow the letter taken from tea
end of picks the last letter of tea
opening picks the first letter of Surrey's

parts.note: a star performer is a pro, a professional

indicators.note: half-heartedly means one of the two middle letters is lost

parts.note: a player who didn't score missed

explanation.surface: A cricket report: after the tea interval, Surrey's opening batsman failed to score.
explanation.walkthrough: Surrey is an English county cricket team; tea is an interval in a cricket match. 'half-heartedly' drops one S from MISSED to leave MISED.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing what was pledged is acting in keeping with an agreement, an idiomatic phrase.

clue.text: Central character in Friends embraced by another giving flowers

indicators.note: the central character means the middle letter of Friends

explanation.surface: One Friends character hugs another, giving flowers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Central character' looks like a lead role in Friends but is the letter at its centre.
explanation.definitionFit: Popular garden blooms are flowers.

clue.text: Ones cut out of type of soft material

indicators.note: cut out of says those letters are removed from the type

parts.note: italic is a style of type
ones are written as I, twice here

explanation.surface: Ones cut out of soft fabric.
explanation.walkthrough: Both I's of ITALIC go.
explanation.definitionFit: A soft mineral ground into powder is a soft material.

clue.text: Tory regulars upset with 'Maoist' individual's followers

explanation.walkthrough: 'upset' rearranges TR, MAOIST and I.
explanation.definitionFit: Copycats follow another's lead, so they are followers in a loose sense.

clue.text: Director coming from Cal., US …

indicators.note: coming from suggests the letters are produced out of the abbreviations, reworked

explanation.surface: A film director who hails from California in the USA.
explanation.walkthrough: George Lucas, maker of Star Wars, really is a Californian.
explanation.definitionFit: George Lucas is a well-known example of a film director.

clue.text: … with whom I'm collaborating in stage production

indicators.note: collaborating suggests the two sets of letters working together, mixed into one

parts.note: whom refers back to the director of the previous clue, 26 across

explanation.walkthrough: The ellipses link this clue to 26; 'collaborating' mixes LUCAS with IM.

clue.text: Locksmith primarily selected instrument to remove front

indicators.note: primarily picks the first letter of selected

parts.note: a bassoon is a woodwind instrument
